name: UK energy price cap
summary: Cap £1,723 a year; Cornwall Insight forecasts £1,999 for January, a 16% rise; Ofgem's January cap is due late November
state: Ofgem's cap for October to December is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household. Cornwall Insight's forecast of 30 Sep puts the January to March 2027 cap at £1,999, up £276 or 16%, inside the Watch band of a 5–20% rise. Some supplier-collated forecasts seen on 8 Nov were higher, above 20%, but rest on weaker predictions and were not confirmed by Cornwall Insight, so the Alert line is not treated as crossed. Ofgem is due to announce the January cap in late November.
for_you: Households on standard variable tariffs pay the cap rate and would see bills rise from 1 Jan if forecasts hold. Those on prepayment, low incomes or in poorly insulated homes are most exposed over winter.

sources.title: Cornwall Insight — 16% price cap rise forecast in January

why: The Ofgem cap sets bills for most UK households — a direct cost-of-living signal.
drivers: Wholesale gas and power prices, network costs, policy levies.

rubric.normal: Typical dual-fuel cap < £1,700/yr and next forecast change < +5%.
